$comment: A fixture-only SPDX map. Deliberately separate from tools/license-audit/spdx-map.json:
adding fixture components to the production map would mean the gate's own test data
ships in the licence report, which is exactly the class of mistake this gate exists to
Every entry has origin 'vcpkg' so nothing is added unless a fixture manifest asks for it.
That keeps each case's baseline empty and its result attributable to one component.

fixture-xapian.$note: Stands in for the real hazard: vcpkg HAS a xapian port, and D4 forbids it.

fixture-bare-gpl-runtime.$note: The GCC runtime identifier with the WITH clause dropped. Must FAIL.

fixture-gcc-runtime.$note: The same identifier, intact. Must PASS -- the control that proves the gate is not simply rejecting everything.

fixture-notice-present.$note: Installed in the fixture tree WITH a NOTICE file -> renders 'yes'.

fixture-notice-absent.$note: Installed WITHOUT a NOTICE file -> renders '**MISSING**'. This is the release blocker, and the whole reason the four states must be distinguishable.

fixture-notice-unbuilt.$note: Absent from the installed tree -> renders 'not checked'. Before I-17 this was also '**MISSING**', which hid the real blocker among routine rows.

fixture-lgpl-lib.$note: Must PASS. LGPL-3.0 contains the letters GPL; a substring test would wrongly reject Qt itself.
